source_book: Sri Chaitanya — FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students, Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Stems restated in our own wording; the mathematics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy. Exponent convention: simple exponents use Unicode superscripts (x², x⁴, eˣ, k xⁿ); compound exponents that have no Unicode superscript form are written with a caret and brackets (x^(2/3), e^(−x/3), t^(3/2), a^(1−k) x^k).

questions.stem: Find dy and Δy for y = x² + 3x + 6 when x = 10 and Δx = 0.01.
Find dy and Δy for y = x² + x when x = 10 and Δx = 0.1.
Find dy and Δy for y = 5x² + 6x + 6 when x = 2 and Δx = 0.001.
Find dy and Δy for y = eˣ + x when x = 5 and Δx = 0.02.
Find dy and Δy for y = 1/(x + 2) when x = 8 and Δx = 0.02.
Find the approximate value of ∛999.
Find the approximate value of √82.
Find the approximate value of cos(60° 5′).
questions.notes: Printed in the question list as cos(60⁰.5¹); the angle is 60 degrees 5 minutes.

questions.stem: Find the approximate value of √65.
questions.notes: Printed in the question list with a square-root sign, but the book's own working for this part treats it as a cube root (∛65). Decide which is intended before authoring.

questions.stem: Find the approximate value of ∛7.8.
The side of a square increases by 4%. Find the percentage change in the area of the square.

The time t of one complete oscillation of a simple pendulum of length l is given by T = 2π√(l/g), where g is the gravitational constant. Find the approximate percentage error in T when the percentage error in l is 1%.
questions.notes: The printed stem names the period both t and T in the same sentence.

questions.stem: The side of a square is increased from 3 cm to 3.01 cm. Find the approximate increase in the area of the square.
The diameter of a sphere is measured as 40 cm. If an error of 0.02 cm is made in the measurement, find the approximate errors in the volume and the surface area of the sphere.
The radius of a sphere is increased from 7 cm to 7.02 cm. Find the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere.
Define the relative error and the percentage error of a variable y.
If y = f(x) = k xⁿ, show that the approximate relative error in y is n times the relative error in x, where n and k are constants.

A container is in the shape of an inverted cone of height 8 m and radius 6 m at the top. It is filled with water at the rate of 2 cubic metres per minute. How fast is the height of the water changing when the level is 4 m?
questions.notes: The printed rate reads "2 cubic metre/mm"; per minute is intended.

questions.stem: A container is in the shape of an inverted cone of height 12 cm and radius 6 cm at the top. It is filled with water at the rate of 12 cm³/sec. What is the rate of change of the height of the water level when the tank is filled to 8 cm?
The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of 9 cubic cm/sec. How fast is the surface area increasing when the length of an edge is 10 cm?
The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of 8 cm³/sec. How fast is the surface area increasing when the length of a side is 12 cm?
A point P is moving on the curve y = 2x². The x-coordinate of P is increasing at the rate of 4 units/sec. Find the rate at which the y-coordinate is increasing when the point is at (2, 8).

A stone is dropped into a quiet lake and the ripples move out in circles at a speed of 5 cm/sec. At the instant when the radius of the circular ripple is 8 cm, how fast is the enclosed area increasing?
The radius of a circle is increasing at the rate of 0.7 cm/sec. What is the rate of increase of its circumference?

A balloon which always remains spherical on inflation is being inflated by pumping in 900 cubic centimetres of gas per second. Find the rate at which the radius of the balloon increases when the radius is 15 cm.
The radius of an air bubble is increasing at the rate of 1/2 cm/sec. At what rate is the volume of the bubble increasing when the radius is 1 cm?

The total cost C(x) in rupees of producing x units of an item is C(x) = 0.005x³ − 0.02x² + 30x + 500. Find the marginal cost when 3 units are produced (marginal cost is the rate of change of total cost).
The total revenue in rupees from the sale of x units of a product is R(x) = 3x² + 36x + 5. Find the marginal revenue at x = 5 (marginal revenue is the rate of change of total revenue).
A kind of bacteria grows so that at time t sec there are t^(3/2) bacteria. Find the rate of growth at time t = 4 hours.
questions.notes: The printed stem gives the count in seconds but asks for the rate at t = 4 hours; the book's own working uses t = 4.

questions.stem: A kind of bacteria grows as t³ (t in sec). At what time is the rate of growth of the bacteria 300 bacteria per sec?

A particle is moving along a line according to S = 4t³ − 3t² + 5t − 1, where S is measured in metres and t in seconds. Find the velocity and the acceleration at time t. At what time is the acceleration zero?

A particle moving along a straight line has the relation S = t³ + 2t + 3 connecting the distance S described by the particle in time t. Find the velocity and the acceleration of the particle at t = 4 sec.
The displacement of a particle travelling in a straight line in t seconds is S = 45t + 11t² − t³. Find the time at which the particle comes to rest.
The distance-time formula for the motion of a particle along a straight line is S = t³ − 9t² + 24t − 18. Find when and where the velocity is zero.

A particle is moving in a straight line so that after t seconds its distance s (in cm) from a fixed point on the line is s = f(t) = 8t + t³. Find i) the velocity at time t = 2 sec, ii) the initial velocity, iii) the acceleration at t = 2 sec.
questions.notes: Printed with three roman asks i)–iii) that share one setup and one worked solution, so they are kept as a single question here rather than split into parts.

questions.stem: Find the average rate of change of s = f(t) = 2t² + 3 between t = 2 and t = 4.
If the tangent at any point on the curve x^(2/3) + y^(2/3) = a^(2/3) intersects the coordinate axes in A and B, show that the length AB is a constant.
Show that the equation of the tangent to the curve √x + √y = √a at the point (x₁, y₁) is x·x₁^(−1/2) + y·y₁^(−1/2) = a^(1/2).
At any point t on the curve x = a(t + sin t), y = a(1 − cos t), find the lengths of the tangent, the normal, the subtangent and the subnormal.
Show that the curves y² = 4(x + 1) and y² = 36(9 − x) intersect orthogonally.
Find the angle between the curves y² = 4x and x² + y² = 5.
Find the angle between the curves y² = 8x and 4x² + y² = 32.
Show that the curves 6x² − 5x + 2y = 0 and 4x² + 8y² = 3 touch each other at (1/2, 1/2).
Find the angle between the curves xy = 2 and x² + 4y = 0.
Find the angle between the curves 2y² − 9x = 0 and 3x² + 4y = 0 in the fourth quadrant.
Find the angle between the curves x + y + 2 = 0 and x² + y² − 10y = 0.
Find the angle between the curves x² + 3y = 3 and x² − y² + 25 = 0.
Show that the square of the length of the subtangent at any point on the curve by² = (x + a)³ varies with the length of the subnormal at that point.
Find the value of k so that the length of the subnormal at any point on the curve y = a^(1−k) x^k is constant.
Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = x⁴ − 6x³ + 13x² − 10x + 5 at (0, 5).
Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve xy = 10 at (2, 5).
Find the equation of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = 5x⁴ at the point (1, 5).
Find the equation of the tangent and the normal to the curve y⁴ = ax³ at (a, a).
Show that the tangent at any point θ on the curve x = c sec θ, y = c tan θ is y sin θ = x − c cos θ.
Find the equation of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = 2e^(−x/3) at the point where the curve meets the y-axis.
Find the lengths of the normal and the subnormal at a point on the curve y = (a/2)(e^(x/a) + e^(−x/a)).
Show that at any point (x, y) on the curve y = b e^(x/a): i) the length of the subtangent is constant, ii) the length of the subnormal is y²/a.
questions.notes: Printed with two roman asks i) and ii) that share one curve and one worked solution, so they are kept as a single question here rather than split into parts.

questions.stem: Find the lengths of the subtangent and the subnormal to the curve y = b sin(x/a) at any point.
Find the equations of the normal to the curve y = x² − 4x + 2 at (4, 2).
Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the curve y = x³ + 4x² at (−1, 3).
Find the slope of the normal to the curve x = a cos³θ, y = a sin³θ at θ = π/4.
Show that the length of the subnormal at any point on the curve y² = 4ax is a constant.
Show that the length of the subtangent at any point on the curve y = aˣ (a > 0) is constant.
If the curved surface of a right circular cylinder inscribed in a sphere of radius r is maximum, then the height of the cylinder is √2 r.

From a rectangular sheet of dimensions 30 cm × 80 cm, four equal squares of side x cm are removed at the corners, and the sides are then turned up so as to form an open rectangular box. Find the value of x so that the volume of the box is the greatest.
Find the maximum area of the rectangle that can be formed with a fixed perimeter 20.
Prove that the radius of the right circular cylinder of greatest curved surface area which can be inscribed in a given cone is half of that of the cone.
Find two positive integers x and y such that x + y = 60 and xy³ is maximum.
Find two positive numbers whose sum is 15, so that the sum of their squares is minimum.
Find the absolute maximum value and the absolute minimum value of the function f(x) = x + sin 2x in [0, π].

The profit function P(x) of a company selling x items per day is given by P(x) = (150 − x)x − 1600. Find the number of items that the company should sell to get the maximum profit. Also find the maximum profit.
Find the absolute extremum of f(x) = x² defined on [2, 2].
questions.notes: The printed interval reads [2, 2]; the book's own working uses [−2, 2]. Confirm the interval before authoring.

questions.stem: Find the intervals on which f(x) = x² − 3x + 8 is increasing or decreasing.
State Rolle's theorem and Lagrange's mean value theorem.
questions.notes: The book prints the full statement of both theorems under this single numbered item, with no separate Sol: block; the statements themselves are not reproduced here.

questions.stem: Verify Rolle's theorem for the function f(x) = x² + 4 in [−3, 3].
Verify Rolle's theorem for the function f(x) = x² − 1 on [−1, 1].
Verify Rolle's theorem for the function f(x) = sin x − sin 2x on [0, π].
Verify Rolle's theorem for the function (x² − 1)(x − 2) on [−1, 2]. Find the point in the interval where the derivative vanishes.
Let f(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3). Prove that there is more than one c in (1, 3) such that f′(c) = 0.
Verify Rolle's theorem for f(x) = x(x + 3)e^(−x/2) on [−3, 0].
Verify Rolle's theorem for the function log(x² + 2) − log 3 on (−1, 1).
It is given that Rolle's theorem holds for the function f(x) = x³ + bx² + ax on [1, 3] with c = 2 + 1/√3. Find the values of a and b.
Verify the conditions of Lagrange's mean value theorem for x² − 1 on [2, 3], and find a point c in the interval as stated by the theorem.
Verify the conditions of Lagrange's mean value theorem for sin x − sin 2x on [0, π], and find a point c in the interval as stated by the theorem.
Verify the Lagrange's mean value theorem for the function logₑ x on [1, 2].
questions.notes: Printed as log_e^x, meaning the natural logarithm of x.

questions.stem: Find c so that f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) for f(x) = x² − 3x − 1, a = −11/7, b = 13/7.
Find c so that f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) for f(x) = eˣ, a = 0, b = 1.
On the curve y = x², find a point at which the tangent is parallel to the chord joining (0, 0) and (1, 1).
Show that there is no real number k for which the equation x² − 3x + k = 0 has two distinct roots in [0, 1].
